sentences.text: Cruxicheiros was a large theropod dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic period in England, though the known fossil material is very limited.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is cataloged as WARMS G15770 and consists of a partial right femur.
This animal is distinguished from Megalosaurus by having lower and broader back spines and differences in leg and hip bones.
In 2012, Thomas Holtz estimated the length of Cruxicheiros at 9 meters, or 29.5 feet.

The type species C. newmanorum was described by Roger Benson and Jonathan Radley in 2010 after remains were discovered in the early 1960s at Cross Hands Quarry near Little Compton, Warwickshire, England.
In 2010, researchers recognized that the Cross Hands Quarry fossils differed from those previously attributed to Megalosaurus.

The genus name Cruxicheiros combines Latin and Greek words for 'cross' and 'hand' to reference the Cross Hands Quarry locality, while the species name newmanorum honors the Newman family, who owned the quarry.
Cruxicheiros is classified as a tetanuran, a group of dinosaurs that includes theropods like Tyrannosaurus and Spinosaurus.
Due to classification uncertainties, Cruxicheiros is classified as Tetanurae incertae sedis, meaning its exact position within the group remains unclear.
The fossils date to the lower Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic, approximately 167 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
The time range for Cruxicheiros is the Bathonian stage, from 168.2 to 165.3 million years ago.
